# zsytri_rook

> Computes the inverse of a complex symmetric matrix using the factorization computed by `zsytrf_rook`.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zsytriRook from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zsytri_rook';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zsytri_rook( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, IPIV, strideIPIV, WORK ) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'`, must match the factorization |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Factored matrix from `zsytrf_rook` |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices from `zsytrf_rook` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | `IPIV` stride length |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `N` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the details of the factorization are stored as an upper or lower triangular matrix.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular, form is $A = U \, D \, U^T$;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular, form is $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L as computed by ZSYTRF\_ROOK.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the (symmetric) inverse of the original matrix. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the upper triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A below the diagonal is not referenced; if `UPLO = 'L'` the lower triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A above the diagonal is not referenced.
- `IPIV`: Details of the interchanges and the block structure of D as determined by ZSYTRF\_ROOK.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zsytri_rook.strided(
    uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

Computes the inverse of a complex symmetric matrix using the factorization computed by `zsytrf_rook`, using alternative indexing semantics.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'`, must match the factorization |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Factored matrix from `zsytrf_rook` |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` (in complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Pivot indices from `zsytrf_rook` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | Stride length for `IPIV` |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IPIV` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array of length at least `N` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: Specifies whether the details of the factorization are stored as an upper or lower triangular matrix.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular, form is $A = U \, D \, U^T$;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular, form is $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L as computed by ZSYTRF\_ROOK.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the (symmetric) inverse of the original matrix. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the upper triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A below the diagonal is not referenced; if `UPLO = 'L'` the lower triangular part of the inverse is formed and the part of A above the diagonal is not referenced.
- `IPIV`: Details of the interchanges and the block structure of D as determined by ZSYTRF\_ROOK.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, $D(i,i) = 0$; the matrix is singular and its inverse could not be computed.

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zsytri_rook()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZSYTRI_ROOK`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zsytri_rook.f).

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import zsytriRook from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zsytri_rook';

// 1x1 complex symmetric factorization (already factored): A = [4 + i].
const A = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, 1.0 ] );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( [ 0 ] );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 1 );

const info = zsytriRook( 'column-major', 'upper', 1, A, 1, IPIV, 1, WORK );

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'A (inverse):', A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZSYTRI_ROOK`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZSYTRI\_ROOK computes the inverse of a complex symmetric matrix A using the factorization $A = U \, D \, U^T$ or $A = L \, D \, L^T$ computed by ZSYTRF\_ROOK.

</section>
